title: One count names every atom
question: What decides which element an atom is?
hook: Inside every atom sits one number that fixes its identity.
idea: An element is a kind of atom fixed by its number of protons, while neutrons only make isotopes.

beats.prompt: An oxygen atom has 8 protons. A nuclear reaction changes that number. What is the atom afterwards?

choices.label: An atom of a different element
Still oxygen, but a new isotope
choices.feedback: Isotopes differ in neutrons, but here the proton count changed.

choices.label: Still oxygen, since a name never changes
choices.feedback: The proton count defines the element, so changing it changes the element.

beats.explain: Nuclear reactions change an atom's atomic number, and the atomic number is what defines the element.

beats.prompt: match each term to its partner
beats.explain: Each term is tied to the proton count or to what changes around it.

beats.prompt: sort each element into its group
beats.explain: The first 94 elements occur naturally, and those beyond 94 have been produced only artificially.

beats.prompt: one step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Atom X has 8 protons, so it is oxygen.
Atom Y also has 8 protons but more neutrons than X.
Atom Y has more neutrons, so it must be a different element.
So X and Y cannot be the same element.
beats.explain: Atoms with the same proton count but different neutron counts are isotopes of the same element.
